title: Sweet Potato, Baked, No Added Fat

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato (batata) is a starchy root vegetable rich in complex carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals. Baking it without added fat preserves its natural flavor and nutritional profile. It has a sweet taste, soft texture, and can be enjoyed on its own or used in salads, side dishes, and whole‑grain meals.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potato belongs to the Convolvulaceae family and is not related to regular potato.
It is high in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Baking without oil retains more antioxidants than frying.
Sweet potatoes can be grown in tropical, subtropical, and even cooler climates.
In Japan, sweet potatoes are used in desserts such as sakura‑imo cookies.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is a precursor of vitamin A, essential for vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids normal heart and muscle function and helps maintain fluid balance.

items.title: Lower glycemic impact when baked
items.content: Baked sweet potato has a lower glycemic index than boiled, making it more suitable for blood‑glucose control.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Anthocyanins and other phytochemicals protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potato.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: People monitoring carbohydrate intake, such as those with diabetes, should watch portion sizes.

items.title: Watch the skin
items.content: The skin may retain pesticide residues; it is advisable to wash thoroughly or peel.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Baked sweet potato can be eaten plain, added to salads, served as a side to meat or fish, or mashed and used as a filling for sandwiches and wraps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store baked sweet potato in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer keeping, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 3 months.
